title: val vs var
body: What is the difference between `val` and `var` in Kotlin?

options.t: val declares a read-only reference that cannot be reassigned; var can be reassigned

answer: val = read-only reference; var = mutable reference.
explanation: `val` does not make the object immutable: a `val list = mutableListOf()` can still be modified. Prefer val by default.

title: Safe call and Elvis
body: What does `name?.length ?: 0` evaluate to when `name` is null?
explanation: `?.` returns null instead of throwing; the Elvis operator `?:` supplies a default. `!!` asserts non-null and throws if it is null.

title: data classes
body: What does the compiler generate for a Kotlin `data class`?

options.t: equals/hashCode, toString, copy and componentN functions based on the primary-constructor properties

explanation: Only properties in the primary constructor participate. `copy(...)` makes immutable updates easy, which is why data classes are common for UI state in Compose.

title: delay vs Thread.sleep
body: Inside a coroutine, how does `delay(1000)` differ from `Thread.sleep(1000)`?

options.t: delay suspends the coroutine without blocking the thread, freeing it for other coroutines; sleep blocks the thread

explanation: `delay` is also cancellable. Never block the main thread on Android; use suspend functions and switch blocking work to `Dispatchers.IO`.
